newsitem.title: AZERBAIJAN: Foreign investment in Azerbaijan up five fold in 96.
newsitem.headline: Foreign investment in Azerbaijan up five fold in 96.

text.p: Foreign investment in Azerbaijan rose five fold in 1996 to $342 million, the Economy Ministry said on Friday, a foretaste of the huge oil wealth lying under the Caspian Sea.

Azerbaijan has signed $15 billion in contracts with Western and Japanese companies to help develop the vast offshore oil fields, and Deputy Economics Minister Oktay Akhverdiyev said that 80 percent of the investment was in the oil sector.
A Western diplomat said the big jump in investment was evidence "oil money" was at last starting to hit the economy.
"I think we are beginning to witness the start of the influx of the big petro dollars," said the diplomat. He predicted the healthy figures would boost overall confidence in the economy.

Total investment from foreign companies and joint ventures totalled 1.4 trillion manats. Overall investment in the economy including from domestic sources rose 74 percent to 2.65 trillion manats, the Ministry said.
Government investment in the economy fell 54 percent to just 83.5 million manats.
Foreign investment in agriculture totalled $34 million or almost 10 percent of the total. The republic of eight million grows cotton, citrus, and other produce.

Despite Azerbaijan's strong economic potential and a booming small enterprise sector, most people still live in poverty and average wages in state jobs, where millions are still employed, are a meagre average $30 a month.

The predominantly Moslem country is still suffering from the effects of an unresolved conflict with neighbour Armenia over the disputed region of Nagorno-Karabakh, in which it lost 20 percent of its territory before a cease-fire was declared three years ago. ($1=4074 manats)
